questions.prompt: What is the fundamental difference between a Cypress E2E test and a TestBed unit test?

options.text: Cypress tests are always faster
Cypress boots the actual compiled app in a real browser with real clicks, routing, and network calls; TestBed runs components in a simulated, isolated environment
TestBed uses a real browser; Cypress simulates the DOM
They are interchangeable

questions.explanation: Cypress proves a user can complete a flow end to end; TestBed proves a unit behaves correctly in isolation.

options.text: Failed tests are automatically re-run three times
Commands and assertions are automatically retried against the live DOM until they pass or a timeout elapses
Cypress retries the whole spec on network errors
You must manually retry each command

questions.explanation: Auto-retrying until an element is actionable removes the need for arbitrary manual waits and reduces flakiness.

questions.prompt: How do you make an E2E test independent of a live backend for a specific request?

options.text: cy.wait(3000)
Use cy.intercept() to observe or stub the request (optionally with a fixture), alias it, and cy.wait('@alias')
Disable the network in the browser
Use TestBed instead

questions.explanation: cy.intercept stubs the response so the test is deterministic and doesn't depend on real backend data.

questions.prompt: Why should you use data-cy attributes instead of CSS classes or IDs for selectors?

options.text: They render faster
They exist solely for testing and are decoupled from styling/behavior, so redesigns don't silently break tests
Cypress cannot read CSS classes
They improve accessibility

questions.explanation: Dedicated test hooks survive markup and styling refactors that would break class/ID-based selectors.

questions.prompt: Why is cy.wait(3000) considered a bad practice for waiting on a response?

options.text: It is not a valid command
It's slow when the response is fast and still flaky when it's slow; cy.wait('@alias') waits exactly as long as needed
It only works in headless mode
It disables retry-ability permanently

questions.explanation: Aliasing an intercept and waiting on it waits precisely for the request, unlike a hardcoded arbitrary delay.

questions.prompt: Which Cypress API caches authenticated browser state across tests so you don't re-login for every test?
questions.explanation: cy.session() caches cookies/localStorage per session key, keeping large suites fast while assertions stay independent.
